public_rationale: A published model estimates more than one million operational Blackwell packages before the post, which is important contrary evidence. But it relies on deployment assumptions and does not verify the May population. Public deployment lists are incomplete, so a count below one million would not prove Zitron's upper bound either.
limitations: A shipment estimate is not an operational count.
Later installations cannot retroactively contradict a May observation.
Operator and tenant announcements can describe the same GPUs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No more than about one million Blackwell GPUs are actually in service, out of roughly three million shipped.

statement.excerpt: I fundamentally do not believe more than a million — if that! — Blackwell GPUs are actually in service.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: more than a million — if that!
our_interpretation: Read as a factual upper-bound estimate of 1,000,000 physical data center Blackwell GPU packages in service globally.
The exact words supply one million; no additional tolerance is imported from the normalized proposition.
Include operational Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra systems. Exclude consumer cards, future orders, and hardware still being installed.
Use the current May 2026 window through publication, consistent with the surrounding May status checks.
Operational availability counts as in service; continuous full utilization is not required.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete operational inventory or defensible global estimate establishes an upper bound of no more than 1,000,000 packages during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reliable global estimate, or a deduplicated lower bound from verified operational deployments, exceeds 1,000,000 packages during the target period.

evidence.explanation: The article models about 1.9 million operationally clustered packages plus deployments outside large clusters. This is material contrary evidence, but its installation assumptions and earlier reference date prevent treating it as a verified May count.
